displayProperties.subtitle: Emissary of the Nine
displayProperties.description: Former DEO agent from pre-Golden Age Chicago, pulled through time to serve as Emissary of the Nine.
displayProperties.name: Lodi

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Lodi turns to you urgently as you approach. "The Nine wax and wane, like a tide. Something about my relationship to them has changed. Will. Is changing. Heh, sorry! I'm… I'm…" He gasps as the Nine overwhelm him with a vision.

"I'm ten miles outside of Allen, South Dakota. 1960. I eat iodine tablets like popcorn and walk on the deck of a ship that appeared… in the ravine." He snorts, disoriented.

"I'm weightless, like… a coin in midair; a beach after an earthquake, before the tsunami. I—Don't worry, I'm here. I'm with you." He was speaking to you, but then he laughs, suddenly, his context shifting again.

"I'm in Madison, Wisconsin. It's 1929. I think that biplane is the most beautiful thing I've ever seen. I want to be up there." He blinks, and it seems like he finally sees you for a moment.

"The Nine are going to come back, and I'll stop them. They stretched me across time and didn't think I'd learn to use it for myself. Hold infinity in the palm of your hand and eternity in an hour. See?"

"It's 1962… and I'm in Lodi, Wisconsin. I feed ducks on the pond downtown. I drove there. My hands hurt from the cold. Ben's sitting next to me…"

He breathes in shakily, shifting his weight again. "It's years from now. You've learned enough Welsh to do more than just curse. Your accent still needs work."

He looks directly at you, now. "I'm not going anywhere. I'll call you sometime, Guardian."

Lodi greets you with warmth and a little twirl as you admire his scarf, "Hey, what do you think of the new look? Took some doing to find a local tailor who did more than robes, but I finally feel dressed for the job." 
 
The two of you share a silent, thoughtful moment. Weapon and Emissary, connected by a shared fate. But, equally, connected by friendship.

He sobers a little as he continues, "As kind as everyone has been, I can tell the Prophecy is still on their minds. And with good reason. The Outer Nine at work, undermining our reality. They're dead set on escaping Sol, no matter the cost. And if they degrade the integrity of our spacetime enough, they could do it."
 
Lodi frowns at you, deep sympathy in his gaze. "I hate to put yet another crisis on your plate, but these Nine-based distortions are manifesting across Sol causing all kinds of problem. The Vanguard is calling this an all-hands-on-deck situation. Good luck out there."

interactions.flavorLineOne:
As you access the interface, it melds with Rosetta, Rojin's words form in your mind. 

"This is all that is needed to align with the final strangelet."

There is a brief pause as calculations are run and ciphers are drafted. The Altar hums along.

"The Gorge can be accessed. Be wary, Anomaly-Blessed. The automatons that attacked Kepler have made the Gorge their home. Orin, saint of the Anomaly, has already departed to face them. Together, you will prevail."

The Altar of Relativity hums as you approach, and an armament for the Weapon materializes.

Collect your reward for completing all missions on Legendary difficulty.

The Altar of Relativity appears to be a relic of a bygone era—a jump drive converted from pre-Golden Age technology. It's been damaged and repaired with components that are obviously straining to contain the forces surging inside. Ghost remarks, "Singularity stabilizers likely aren't an off-the-shelf item."

The Aionians have been extremely clever and resourceful in assembling this complex device, despite their relative lack of resources. Still, the altar is definitely unstable. Strangelet capsules appear to be the only method of effectively stabilizing the altar, and by extension, the singularity.

As you access the interface, it melds with Rosetta, Rojin's words form in your mind. 

"Anomaly-Blessed, your field work is efficient and thorough. We are fortunate to have found favor with you. With the return of another strangelet, we are able to cull bad data from our hypotheses. We've narrowed your next destination to the Outer Steppes. We are locking the Altar to that strangelet capsule now." 

"Go in certainty."

As you approach the Altar you feel a strange kind of hum. It is not audible, but you can feel it both physically and paracausually within you.
There is also something else there, a new…feeling? It's not anything you've experienced before. It's some kind of resonance beyond the physical and paracausal.
You feel satiated, and yet there is a sense that there is much more to whet your appetite on this planetoid… and elsewhere.
It seems that you've taken your first step into a larger, stranger world.

The language of the interface is indecipherable, but the altar appears to be unpowered. It cannot process a strangelet capsule integration.

Ghost is tracing power transfers around the altar site. The source appears to be dark matter conduits, most likely kept away from the Aionian security zone for safety.

Ghost believes it's possible to restore power.

As you access the interface, it melds with Rosetta, speaking words from an Aionian into your inner voice. 

"Anomaly-Blessed. I am Rojin, the Altar's technician, and the one honored to deliver what help we can. We offer, in awe, our findings to aid you. Should you see fit, your impressive drone will receive actionable data to locate strangelet capsules, and use the Altar's relativistic connection with them as a cipher to pass into the cordoned regions of Kepler. With our current integrations and research, you will gain access to the Central Academy and the Exile's Accord."

There is a brief pause as Ghost accepts the data transmission.

"Most gracious, Anomaly-blessed. Transfer commencing."

"We shall continue our research into the other stolen strangelets. With further integrations, the remaining capsules will increase synchronicity with the Altar and allow us to impose a shifted perspective that ignores the cordons by our observation of the strangelet beyond them. It is a delicate alignment, but our efforts can only improve through iteration."
Track your Fabled exploration progress and strangelet capsule collection.
Collect strangelet capsules in World Tier: Mythic and integrate them at the Altar of Relativity.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
A pre-recorded message from Banshee-44 starts playing at your approach.

"Hey, Guardian. I'm sending you something. Took me a while to figure out what that rifle of yours was doing. You know, the… strange one. Quicksilver something. It's the nanite colony in it. They're working to calibrate to your combat style, but you and the weapon aren't what their base programming expects, so it's taking a while. I wrote up a little code to start the handshake off on the right foot. You'll want to take it through its paces where you are in Neomuna first. Let me know when you've matched the metrics."

He's included a quick summary of numerical objectives. And also a note to himself, for when you bring it back to him.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Aghol. Totality Armorer. And you're the Lightbearer who's raised such a ruckus around the place."

The Armorer eyes you up and down. "Well, I don't mind a bit of a ruckus myself. There are plenty of abandoned drop pods scattered across Sol's old battlefields. Easy enough to recover and repurpose as artillery."

"Even Guardians know, nothing outside the pod survives contact with the pod." Aghol laughs loudly, and hands you a beacon.

Armorer Aghol clears his throat. "Got some more legalese for you, Lightbearer. You ready?"

"'The Totality Division is grateful for your continued support. The rewards promised you are being held in escrow by Spider. If you have any issues with the delivery, we request that you take it up with him. With regards from Enforcer Rao."

"Glad I don't have to write that stuff myself," Aghol says. "But we mean it."

Aghol scratches his chin. "Looking for a Syndicate to ally with? I won't say we couldn't use you, Guardian. And you couldn't do better than the Totality Division.

"One thing about the Division is, Rao doesn't brook any nonsense. We won't mess with your Glimmer. We share resources accordingly. What am I gonna do with a Praxic Blade, cut my hand off? Any mods come in, they're earmarked for you—if you earn 'em."

"I'll see you back here soon, yeah?"
Deposit Dark Matter Ingots at the Totality Division War Chest to earn Reputation with this Syndicate. Earn Renegade Abilities, Praxic Blade modifications, gear, and currency.

displayProperties.name: Ikora Rey

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"There are few feelings quite like coming back home. What do you feel when you arrive home? Is it happiness, relief, nostalgia for what you left behind?

"I recall one homecoming after a lengthy mission. I stepped into my bedroom and was confronted by, to my surprise, unease. It was so empty. The walls, the floors, my space was simply that… space. Being away for so long gave me new perspective, reminded me of the importance of creating a place where you can truly be comfortable, truly yourself. I resolved never to neglect that need again.

"Close your eyes, envision your home. Whatever peculiar sense comes to you, meditate on that, Guardian."

"I once read a poem of a man whose soul was incinerated after staring at the sun for too long. Far from dead, he lived the rest of his days in communion with the universe itself, blessing the people of his small village with wisdom beyond peer.

"A strange tale, but one I find myself relating to after particularly… intense lessons from the Traveler in meditation.

"So, Guardian," Ikora says and smiles, "what wisdom might you share with me?"

"Hello again, Guardian. The Traveler has many lessons to teach us. If only we were all so receptive to them as you have been.

"In my quieter moments, I begin to think I may understand just what these lessons mean. Yet the moment I concentrate on them, they slip away.

"Though these moments may confuse us, the pursuit is worth the frustration that can follow. Meditate on that today."

"I was out for a walk this morning when I heard two children laughing. I didn't think much of it. I kept on my way. What was so funny? I don't know; I'll never know.

"Yet as I've continued to reflect on that moment, I realized… I don't remember the last time I laughed. Truly, uncontrollably laughed.

"The weight of our responsibilities can sap the joy out of the mundane, yet some of the deepest insights one can have come packaged in jokes.

"Don't lose your sense of humor, Guardian. Meditate on something that makes you smile today."

"Time to meditate once again. It may seem repetitive, but ritual is essential. I learned that when I was studying under Osiris. 

"Osiris has always had his head in the clouds. Cosmic priorities, galactic concerns, universal woes. When he was driven out of the City, one of the major complaints lodged against him was his absence. The people of this City did not see his contribution, didn't think he was worth the trouble of the zealots that gathered round him.

"I like to think I got a glimpse of the real Osiris. The Osiris that could never lead a cult of personality. The Osiris who eats, breathes, and sleeps, however seldom." Ikora cracks a smile.

"There was one thing Osiris never failed to do day in, day out. With careful precision, he prepared himself a cup of tea at exactly the same time, in exactly the same manner. I'm certain that a man who so dutifully observed this tradition could never have lost his head in the clouds.

"Don't lose sight of the here and now, Guardian. The future can't exist without it."

"You have become a truly formidable force. This power makes it easy to forget our true purpose.

"Our Light is a beacon, and though we may be forced to wield it as a weapon, battle is not its true purpose.

"What is its true purpose? I'm not sure I can say with certainty, but I feel it is far deeper than any single word can contain.

"Meditate on this, Guardian. Sometimes uncertainty yields the greatest insights."

"The Light is a beautiful thing, a privilege. One that so many will never experience the way you and I do.

"Why are we so lucky? Many ask, but there's never an answer. I prefer to think about why so many are unlucky, passed up for the privilege which you and I take for granted.

"How many times have I died? How many second chances at life have I been given? I can scarcely count. Yet so many live with the knowledge that they only get one.

"If you're hoping for a message, a point. I'm afraid I don't have one. It feels wrong, but it is."

"Looking into the sky, I can't help but see all we've lost. People, perspectives, whole planets. I began this fight so long ago, I've lost more than I had when I started.

"Yet the fight will continue because it must. We will lose much, much more.

"Prepare yourself for that. Meditate on what you've lost. Feel it in your fingers, then let it go."

"It can be difficult to manage the weight of expectations. The expectations placed on us by our roles as Guardians, how we serve those who need us, but also those expectations we foist on ourselves.

"You have taken on even more power, unlocked even more potential. These new abilities may not sit right at first. Don't lose faith if not everything comes naturally.

"We all falter under the weight of expectations. Pick yourself back up, and carry them again tomorrow."

"You and I have seen our share. We have our stories, our successes, our regrets. A tapestry of beautiful experience.

"We are united by strange forces which we barely understand, and they afford us a life we could never have dreamed of.

"Through the challenge, through the pain, through the worry for tomorrow, we must always recognize this truth:

"It is good to be a Guardian. Don't forget it."

"Welcome home, Guardian. I heard your journey to the Last City was an eventful one," Ikora says as she gazes at the Traveler. "It may not feel like it now, but the tribulations you faced were a blessing." She turns to address you; her stare is piercing.

"A Guardian's path is one of hardship and peril. The Traveler's gifts pave the way, but the road is still a hard one to walk."

"But you need not walk it alone. The Vanguard is here for you, as are your fellow Guardians in the Last City."

She hands you a small lacquered box.

"Accept help where you can find it, Guardian. Our Light shines brighter when we're together."

displayProperties.description: Once a Lightbearer, Eris Morn descended into the Hellmouth of the Moon where she lost her fireteam, her Ghost, and her Light to the Hive.
displayProperties.name: Eris Morn

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"This… communes with me. And I know it… I know him. This is what remains of dear Omar. Tortured by the Hive. I knew not that he would be transformed by Crota's twisted experiments…

"I am sorry I couldn't save you, friend. In life, you may have been unable to escape their grasp. But you will have your vengeance yet."

Eris has kept in her possession one of Omar's greatest assets: his beloved Machine Gun. Eris empowers it with the spirit of Omar, and grants it to you.
Eris takes the gift from you, looks at it a moment, and then smiles very faintly. She thanks you and wishes you well.

The efforts of Guardians within the Black Garden seem to have unlocked the Unknown Artifact. It now provides communications from something… sinister. Eris warns us not to bow to it but believes the Artifact too valuable to dispose of.

Collect any further communications it sends, but remain cautious. There is little here to trust.

headerDisplayProperties.description: Speak to Eris regarding discoveries made within the Black Garden.
headerDisplayProperties.name: The Infection Runs Deep

interactions.flavorLineOne: Somehow, within the Pit of Heresy, the remaining Daughters of Crota managed to revive Zulmak, strengthened and protected by the Darkness within the crystal. With their rejection of sword logic, Crota's daughters have become far more dangerous. You may have scared them off for now, but there is no doubt they will seek revenge.

headerDisplayProperties.description: Speak to Eris in Sanctuary.
headerDisplayProperties.name: Lingering Torment

interactions.flavorLineOne:
It is possible you've done a terrible thing in caging such power. But terrible things have forced your hand. Unleash your fury across the system, until all who consider themselves the fever dreams of our eternal torment understand. You, when pushed, are the only nightmare worth fearing.

You have crafted a weapon of corruption and doom, powered by the stolen might of the Hive's wicked Song.

Unleash its fury upon your enemies. Become death.

"A phantom of my deceased fireteam member Sai Mota haunts me. It is only a trick of the Pyramid."

From the Nightmare of Crota, you received an unknown object that harbors a dark energy. You leave it with Eris Morn so she can unearth its secrets.

In the meantime, the Moon hosts further mysteries to uncover regarding entering the Pyramid. The Hive seem to be exhibiting strange behavior that may be related.

Investigate the strange Hive behavior near the Scarlet Keep.

While Eris is pleased that you defeated the Undying Mind, she warns you not to let your guard down. There are greater threats on the horizon. She urges you to keep those threats at the forefront of your mind—and prepare accordingly.

headerDisplayProperties.description: Eris Morn has heard of your victory over the Undying Mind and wishes to speak to you. Visit her in Sanctuary on the Moon.
headerDisplayProperties.name: Eris Morn

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Memories buried, only now remembered. Years ago, I recall reports of music, of a hymn murmured by Deathsingers beneath the Moon's surface."

"This is a song of destruction, our destruction. I believe we can harness this power and turn it against the Hive."

"There is a mystery here," Eris says softly. She turns the tablet around in her hands. "A memory stirs. I think…no."

She shakes her head. "The runes indicate the Anchor of Light. You may begin there to unravel the threads of this enigma."

Make your way to the Anchor of Light on the Moon to begin this journey.

"This skull is only the first instrument in our new symphony. With its guidance, we will twist the Hive's tainted lullaby to our will. But first we must bind its gifts. Scour the Moon. Bring me the bones of the damned."

Hunt enemies on the Moon. Gather bones for Eris by completing the activities she requires.

"The Pyramid wastes no time—a phantom of Toland has arrived with every intention of distracting me. It will not work."

During Eris's time in the Hellmouth, she discovered many Hive curios. All that remained was an ancient talisman pulsating with Hive magic. Now, the union between the talisman and the Essence of Despair has yielded a powerful tool in the fight against the Nightmares.

Take this piece of Dreambane armor and use it to hunt the Nightmare of Omnigul.

"It appears the screams of Sai's phantom have brought forth another burden for me to bear—the phantom of Vell Tarlowe."

As the Nightmare of Omnigul swept through camp, Eris noticed a strange reaction from the Essence of Despair. Upon further investigation, it appears the Essence can be of use in fighting these Nightmares. But first, it must be cleansed of any dark energy.

Take the Essence of Despair and purify it any way you can. Then, return to Eris Morn.

Eris believes that whatever these things are, they want nothing more than to destroy everything we hold dear.

Eris takes the Unknown Artifact from you. She desires to study it in hopes of making sense of all that you saw within the Pyramid.

You now stand at the precipice of the future. The Pyramid holds many secrets within. Lift the veil, and find a way inside. Look for something within—anything that might help humanity fight the oncoming storm.

Return to the Enduring Abyss with a full set of Dreambane armor equipped, and find a way inside the Pyramid.

"The phantom of Eriana-3 now haunts me alongside the rest. They are a burden that weighs heavy on my mind."

The Cryptoglyph must be used to empower the Lectern of Enchantment near Eris. In tandem with the cleansed Essence of Anguish, this will yield another piece of Dreambane armor.

Empower the Lectern of Enchantment with the Cryptoglyph before setting off to hunt the remaining Nightmares.

More Nightmare Essences are required to craft the remaining three pieces of Dreambane armor.

"It is no surprise that the Pyramid now inflicts the phantom of Omar Agah upon me. The Pyramid will do anything to stop us from getting inside."

Hashladûn has been disposed of, and with her death comes a path to victory: the Hive Cryptoglyph.

Travel to the Hellmouth and locate the Catacombs within. Hashladûn's Cryptoglyph lies inside for the taking.

You have acquired further Nightmare Essences but are out of Hive curios with which to create more Dreambane armor.

After discovering the Hive's ability to shield themselves from the Nightmares, Eris learned of a dark power possessed by the Hive inside the Scarlet Keep. This power may be our answer to how they've protected themselves—and our key to creating more Dreambane armor.

Investigate the dark power within the Scarlet Keep.

The strange Hive rituals within Sorrow's Harbor have proven to be only the tip of the iceberg. Eris believes the remaining Daughters of Crota are sacrificing Nightmares to obtain their dark energy. What the Daughters are using them for, she does not know. But all signs point beneath the Harbor itself.

Search Sorrow's Harbor for the entrance to the Pit of Heresy.

Your success in entering the Pyramid and obtaining the Unknown Artifact has prepared us more than ever for the looming threat of the Darkness. But this is no time for rest.

- Help Eris dispel the phantoms of her lost fireteam

- Hunt Nightmares at higher difficulties

- Uncover the secrets of the Moon's Lost Sectors

- Find further Nightmare Essences spread across the Moon

- Gather Phantasmal Fragments to choose Essences from the Lectern of Enchantment

headerDisplayProperties.description: Speak to Eris.
headerDisplayProperties.name: A Persistent Threat

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Eriana-3 was the Praxic Warlock who led our fireteam of six into the Hellmouth and… unknowingly… to our doom. I do not blame her, Guardian. During the Great Disaster, Crota snuffed out the love in her heart and left only venom. In the end, before she lost her life in the Oversoul Throne, Eriana-3 came to regret her haste for vengeance."

Reclaim the true memory of Eriana-3 for Eris Morn.

Begin by recovering stolen treasures from Lunar Scavengers beneath the surface of the Moon.

"Our focus is to be shifted. We created a wake when we destroyed Hashladûn and took the Cryptoglyph—and that wake has grown and grown. Hashladûn's two remaining sisters appear to have picked up where her foul plans left off. Once again, strange Hive rituals have commenced near the Keep. We must tame these plans before they become too grand to handle."

Investigate the Hive rituals in Sorrow's Harbor.

"Of the six of us who descended into the pit, the Hunter Omar Agah surely suffered the most terrible fate. Captured alive by the Heart of Crota, Omar's Light was cut away from him in small bits, used to feed and coax newborn creatures from their cocoons. I will never forget the sounds he made as he died."

Reclaim the true memory of Omar Agah for Eris Morn.

Begin by defeating a powerful Hive Wizard using Super abilities.

"Sai Mota was a Hunter who walked with us on our doomed journey for vengeance against Crota. Most of us did not make it, however. She… fell to the Wizard Omnigul, laughing as she died."

Reclaim the true memory of Sai Mota for Eris Morn.

Begin by searching for the system core vault within the K1 Revelation Lost Sector.

"Toland, the mad. Toland, the cursed. The exiled. And finally, the Shattered. He knew more about the Hive and the 'song' of their Deathsingers than any other. Had Eriana-3 questioned his convenient obsession further before recruiting him to our fireteam, things might have been different. But fate is fate. That he could not control."

Reclaim the true memory of Toland for Eris Morn.

Search the Moon's surface for a Hive Trove Guardian obscuring a hidden path.

"Vell Tarlowe was one of the strongest Titans I've ever known. A member of the Pilgrim Guard, but even his Light was smothered by the waves of Thrall that rush beneath the surface of the Moon. He underestimated them… and he paid the price."

Reclaim the true memory of Vell Tarlowe for Eris Morn.

Begin by completing an active replayable story mission on the Moon.

"How long have we lived without questioning the nature of our crafted existence? Do not mistake my curiosity for a turnabout of loyalty—the Light has given us life, while these things have given us only deceit and dysfunction. But… perhaps we are not as in control as we'd like to be. After all, what is the point of life without liberty?"

Press Accept to receive a mysterious transmission.

headerDisplayProperties.description:
Whispers flow from the Unknown Artifact, creating sinister messages picked up by Eris Morn.

Someone or something is attempting to speak to us.
headerDisplayProperties.name: Whispers in the Dark

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"You must see this… The implication is an alteration of the very fabric of reality as we know it. Who or what has life descended from? It cannot be what these transmissions suggest. But at the same time, perhaps maybe… I believe you must judge for yourself."

Press Accept to receive a mysterious transmission.

headerDisplayProperties.description:
Whispers flow from the Unknown Artifact, creating sinister messages picked up by Eris Morn.

Someone or something is attempting to speak to us.
headerDisplayProperties.name: Whispers in the Dark

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"What first appeared as nonsense and trickery has begun to reveal itself. Certainly we are being manipulated through these interactions, though there is an honesty here… a spark of truth that speaks louder than I sought to allow. I will give it some credence—but please, do not let my curiosity infect your truths."

Press Accept to receive a mysterious transmission.

headerDisplayProperties.description:
Whispers flow from the Unknown Artifact, creating sinister messages picked up by Eris Morn.

Someone or something is attempting to speak to us.
headerDisplayProperties.name: Whispers in the Dark

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"These words contain an ancient and unknown power. They are something beyond manipulative ruminations. There is a cry within them, one that seeks to be heard, lost in a sea that only dampens their truths. We must let them be heard. It may be our only way to prepare for whatever comes next."

Press Accept to receive a mysterious transmission.

headerDisplayProperties.description:
Whispers flow from the Unknown Artifact, creating sinister messages picked up by Eris Morn.

Someone or something is attempting to speak to us.
headerDisplayProperties.name: Whispers in the Dark

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"We know we should keep ourselves from these deceptive interactions, but what we are learning here are truths previously untold. They are asking to be understood. To be known. Perhaps their intentions are far less black-and-white than we first assumed. As always, stay cautious… but perhaps we should not stray from learning the secrets of the universe."

Press Accept to receive a mysterious transmission.

headerDisplayProperties.description:
Whispers flow from the Unknown Artifact, creating sinister messages picked up by Eris Morn.

Someone or something is attempting to speak to us.
headerDisplayProperties.name: Whispers in the Dark

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Their transmissions have ceased. But I am confident it is not the end of their trechery. You have continued to stand by me through it all. A beacon of light shining through their forced darkness. For that, I have only this remaining message to give."

Press Accept to receive Eris's message.

headerDisplayProperties.description:
Whispers continue to flow from the Unknown Artifact, but their transmissions have stopped.

Eris, however, has a message for you.
headerDisplayProperties.name: Whispers in the Dark

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Please do not think I have strayed from the Light. Understand that first and foremost, knowledge will save us all. Know thy enemy… a cliché, yes. But for a reason. Please realize this enemy—it is not like our other enemies. It fights with a different kind of force. Were we to simply shoot at it, I fear we would never stand a chance. Sometimes you must accept another's truth to understand their weakness. I hope you'll join me on this journey."

Press Accept to receive a mysterious transmission.

headerDisplayProperties.description:
Whispers flow from the Unknown Artifact, creating sinister messages picked up by Eris Morn.

Someone or something is attempting to speak to us.
headerDisplayProperties.name: Whispers in the Dark

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Perhaps what we think of ourselves is simply within our minds, not in our makeup. Perhaps what built us is not what we thought it was. Always prescribing rationale to the chaos. Always finding light within the dark. Never considering the possibility of a parallel existence within the very building blocks of life. The cards are not what we thought they were. But still we must play the game."

Press Accept to receive a mysterious transmission.

headerDisplayProperties.description:
Whispers flow from the Unknown Artifact, creating sinister messages picked up by Eris Morn.

Someone or something is attempting to speak to us.
headerDisplayProperties.name: Whispers in the Dark

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Somewhere in the space between it all… between the truth and the lies, between power and weakness, between day and night, I have lived. In the gray. I believed not by choice, but by force. Chaos reigned, and I embraced it, but ultimately sought to regain equilibrium. Now, however, if these stories are true, I wonder… Perhaps there is only chaos. Perhaps it is the only thing worth embracing."

Press Accept to receive a mysterious transmission.

headerDisplayProperties.description:
Whispers flow from the Unknown Artifact, creating sinister messages picked up by Eris Morn.

Someone or something is attempting to speak to us.
headerDisplayProperties.name: Whispers in the Dark

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Pay little attention to the false equivalencies within these messages. They seek to use familiarity to lead us into the darker recesses of our minds… Do not misunderstand—these are certainly fascinating places to explore. But we do so at the risk of giving ourselves to something without our best interests at heart."

Press Accept to receive a mysterious transmission.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Sinister transmissions seep out from our Unknown Artifact. Their intentions are anything but pure. Place your eyes upon them only if you seek to find truths among the lies."

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Mechanic Deoriks waves you over, a stack of datapads heaped precariously in the crook of one elbow.

"Good news, latest shipment's just in. Riliks told me to reserve a portion of it for you in thanks for your efforts last week. Spider's holding onto it for you."

She clacks her mandibles. "Don't love Spider getting his greasy hands on our stuff, but Riliks says we gotta pick our battles sometimes. And in this case, victory is meditating on the lovely warm memory of Spider's barge exploding."

Deoriks flags you down with a wave of a datapad.

"You're the Guardian Vixis has been talking to? Well, I guess if you're helping him out, you're all right for a Lightbearer," she says.

"You ever ride a Pike? A Falcon's like that, but more. I can list every component we use in 'em and where we get 'em, but I don't want to keep you when you've got Imperium goons to squash.

"Remember—if you're not scared you're about to crash, you're not going fast enough."

The Pikers' quartermaster Deoriks beckons you over with a confiding air.

"You know us, Guardian. Do you want the frontier run by a military force with Imperium ties? Or a bunch of soup that likes to gamble? Pikers are the only answer."

She leans in. "Listen, Riliks is a weird one, but they've got vision. I've never regretted joining up. I'll take this gang over any House you could name. 

"We've got the best tech, the best perks, and—let's be honest here—the best company. Ride with the Pikers, Guardian. You won't regret it."
Deposit Dark Matter Ingots at the Pikers War Chest to earn Reputation with this Syndicate. Earn Renegade Abilities, Praxic Blade modifications, gear, and currency.

interactions.flavorLineOne: "We have to be ready for anything." Ghost is uncharacteristically grim. "We'll need every advantage we can get to stop the Witness. Now's not the time to hold back. For you, or me. Whatever happens, we either win or we go down fighting." He looks at you, determined. "Together."

"The final days are ahead of us. The clock is ticking, and the fate of the entire universe is at stake." Ghost looks to you, confident and ready for anything. "Guardians make their own fate, and so do Ghosts. Let's get out there and show the Witness what legends truly are." 

You have completed the Legendary campaign. Please select your reward.

"Guardian, I think we're in completely new territory. Light and Darkness are powerful but unbalanced. We need to unify them into one coherent force, or they'll tear us apart.

The Dyadic Prism resonates. It's leading us to unify Light and Darkness."

Ghost's shell buzzes with excitement.

"Guardian, look! No, feel! We've beaten back the Witness's corruption, and the Traveler is healing. The work you—we—no, everyone has done has helped save the Traveler! After everything, I never thought I'd get to help it like this. We were only a small piece of it, but it feels good, doesn't it?"

The collective work of Guardians to heal the Traveler has unlocked the following reward:
Apply this catalyst to the Exotic Fusion Rifle Tessellation.

headerDisplayProperties.name: The Final Shape + Annual Pass Catalyst

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Guardian, I think we're in completely new territory. Light and Darkness are powerful but unbalanced. We need to unify them into one coherent force, or they'll tear us apart.

The Dyadic Prism resonates. It's leading us to unify Light and Darkness."

Even though your last confrontation with the Witness ended in retreat, you were still able to land a devastating blow—proof that your newfound powers are strong enough to defeat it. 

The Witness was not the only one wounded by the encounter. Ghost's condition has rapidly deteriorated, and it's clear to you that he's only holding himself together so the two of you can finish this. 

And you'll need the Traveler's full power behind you to do so. 

Work with allied reinforcements to weaken and sever the Witness's hold on the Traveler. Only then will you be able to use your mastery over both Light and Darkness to unmake humanity's most ancient enemy.

The Witness is gone. 

 But so is Cayde-6, who sacrificed his Light to restore your Ghost's. He bet it all on you. Still, Ghost can feel Cayde's presence. It's as though he and every other Ghost and every other Guardian that came before you are connected by the Traveler's Light. The Witness sought to give meaning to the universe, but Cayde has shown you that meaning—like fate—is yours to choose. His last act was to ensure that you and your Ghost will have a future together in a way that he and Sundance could not. What will you do with it?

Standing on the ledge of the old Tower, you bring Ghost out.

He hovers in front of you, light blinking. "Guardian, I've been doing a lot of thinking. I know I haven't been very enthusiastic about using Darkness in the past, but…at this point, we can't afford to ignore something that can help.

"I've been tracking leads on potential sources of power, both Light and Dark. I still think we should be careful, but…"

He dips slightly in the air. "I think it's what the Traveler wants."
Complete Pathfinder objectives, Overthrow, Lost Sectors, and Cysts, and open chests in the Pale Heart to increase your Ghost reputation and earn rewards.

displayProperties.description: Data Architect Extraordinaire
displayProperties.name: Quinn Laghari

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"I guess it isn't too outrageous to think a Strider would protect anyone in need. Even a Vex. If the Occlusion wanted to hurt us, it could have. Instead, it just seems to like its independence and some quiet. And I know I like my naps, so I'm feeling a little connection, you know?"

"It sent a big old compressed data packet in one quick burst, right before it went quiet again. Back to sleep, I guess. This was in the header:

SELF=output.vex :: output.soteria // SUBJECT=paracausal.hero // I ENDURE. GRATITUDE.

"This is going to make for some interesting research papers in the next few years… Anyway. This doc was right at the top of the other files, not encrypted like the rest. Here's the text: 

URGENT: SATURN VI CONTAINS VITAL INFORMATION. ENEMY OF WITNESS ON TITAN. IF STILL LIVING PRESERVATION PARAMOUNT. DO NOT WASTE TIME.

"It must have hauled some information out of the Vex databases. Or… our databases? Both? Ugh. I'm going to be forever figuring out the rest. Still, hope that's helpful to what you've got going on." 

Quinn's gratitude is genuine. "I won't forget everything you've done for me. And for the city. We owe you a lot, friendly space zombie. You're welcome here anytime. Oh, and here! Nimbus said you like weapons, so I dug this out of the archive for you. Don't worry—it's not fragile."

"So it turns out—no shocker—Bluejay found the Occlusion from the first Strider's records. I've got a bigger issue for you, though."

"My 'Occlusion' data crawler accidentally expanded to scan Shadow Legion radio chatter. It returned a hit. The Cabal discovered a new Vex operation looking for the Occlusion and ordered their troops to steer clear."

"So the Vex aren't afraid of the Occlusion. They want it, and they're tunneling into the CloudArk to find it."

"My data crawler's running hot! Maelstrom accessed the Occlusion a lot. She called it a 'simulation echo.' But it's not a saved file. It's hidden code in the CloudArk! She found it in Cloud Strider Bluejay's notes, so… you know. Kinda need his archive restored."

"So I need you to restore Stargazer's records." Quinn's avatar radiates cheer. "All you need to do is sort of 'vibe' with Stargazer… the city's most famous explorer."

"The short version is, you must have tapped into some kind of connection with Siegebreaker. Emotional, experiential… something strong, whatever it was. So my theory is, to do the same thing with Stargazer, the best place to start is emulating them somehow, looking for that same connection. I could expound on the psychological and philosophical theories if you want. There's a lot of interesting research into the nature of consciousness, especially given the CloudArk… Maybe the city's belief in the Cloud Striders helped you anchor the memorial? Or maybe you're just that good at magic archaeology."

Quinn is overjoyed to have one monument back, and that scientific mind is hard at work on the best ways to get you to reconstruct the rest. Between your Strand capabilities and her historical knowledge, she's pretty clearly hoping you'll be able to restore all of the lost records. There's a whole city invested in the history of their heroes, after all. And ideally in the process, you can solve the mystery of the Vex attack.

headerDisplayProperties.name: Welcome to the Hall of Heroes

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"I found Stargazer's algorithm in the data you recovered, except it's not an algorithm. They called it 'The Occlusion.' Love this stuff. My data crawler also pulled some old library records, showing who else accessed Stargazer's archive back in the day. Maelstrom!
She was the greatest military mind in history AND she's one of our smashed servers. It can't be a coincidence."

"If this 'Occlusion' spooked the Vex, maybe Maelstrom kept a backup of it on her server. She was a warrior, so go start some fights!"

"This… I must have made a mistake." Quinn's crisis of faith is obvious in her voice. "The Cabal data says the Vex are searching for a Vex Mind inside our network? But that would mean the Strider helped hide it and keep it secret, even from the Council! From me! Not that I was even born yet, but it still feels… personal. We're not supposed to be a city of secrets."

Quinn's holographic form moves back and forth restlessly. "Okay. Okay, let's think this through. The Strider must have had a reason to do this, even if we can't see it yet. Maybe her memorial can tell us more. Think you can fix it?"

Quinn believes your Strand powers can restore the destroyed memorials of Neomuna's heroes by finding connection with those previous Cloud Striders, perhaps based on their unique places in Neomuni history.

Stargazer—originally a mathematician named Laminak Li—was an explorer. Their legacy revolves around witnessing grand events and recovering lost treasure.

Engage in Terminal Overload activities to begin bonding with this legacy.

It all goes back to the first Cloud Strider, a woman named Mikaela Julaha. "We don't know enough, unfortunately. Record-keeping was spotty back then. We were fighting just to survive, so no one was keeping receipts we could sift through centuries later. What I do know from context clues is that the Strider was the first person to use the Occlusion, and the only person who really knew what it is—except maybe the Vex, apparently. All I know for sure is she never set out to be a hero. She just wanted a safe home, where her kids didn't need to fight every day just to survive."

The Shadow Legion have uncovered a Vex tunneling operation, but the comms chatter Quinn has been able to pick up hasn't been very specific apart from that. The Shadow Legion have been ordered away from the operation, but that still leaves many places in Neomuna where the Vex could be working, and the Shadow Legion might yet be in active retreat.

Sweep through the areas where Vex and Shadow Legion are fighting to rule out those areas, and collect encrypted data from them to analyze and further narrow down where the Vex operation could be. With any luck, the chase will help you bond with the Strider's legacy—but the defense of the city is the most vital goal.  

Unlock a Terminal Overload Key Chest in each occupied area of Neomuna to begin tracking the Vex tunneling operation.

A strange clue connects the Cloud Striders whose memorials were destroyed: Something they refer to as "The Occlusion." What it is or why the Vex want it remains a mystery, though.

Quinn asks you to try restoring the memorial to Sedderik Assur, the Cloud Strider known as Maelstrom. She was a war hero and tactician, so engaging the enemy and stockpiling supplies seem like the next logical steps.

Defend the city by participating in patrols and public events and loot chests to begin bonding with this legacy.

Details on the Occlusion trace back to Conrad Jain, the Cloud Strider who went by Bluejay. He was a former hacker and criminal who ultimately turned his skills toward saving the city and transforming the CloudArk into the virtual world it is today. But with so much network security surrounding Bluejay's legacy, you'll need Nimbus's help getting access.

Visit Nimbus to begin bonding with this legacy.

"Well, this is a mess," Quinn says, indicating the broken memorials behind her. "But at least you kept the Veil safely in Neomuna! You know, it keeps the CloudArk running; we'd be lost without it. And on top of that, we haven't even scratched the surface on what it has to say about Darkness."

"Most immediately urgent is the broken memorials. The battle with Calus brought CloudArk security briefly offline, and some anomalous signal patterns were broadcast unsecured, coinciding almost perfectly in timing with the activation of the Veil. The Vex broke in immediately afterward, and destroyed five specific Cloud Strider memorials before retreating. Clearly a precision strike, but the question is, why?"

Cloud Strider memorials house all of their personal and professional records for future generations to study. Quinn is sure the answer is somewhere in the destroyed files. With any luck, Ghost's advanced sensors can help her pull data from the destroyed memorial servers and get a clearer picture of why the Vex undertook such a risky attack.

"Go take a look around the Hall first, all right? Get a good picture of how this place is in the parts that aren't on fire, learn a little about Neomuna that doesn't involve sabotage or explosions. Then you can circle back to the memorials, do some scans, and hopefully blow my socks off with what you and Ghost can pick up."

Explore the Hall of Heroes to learn more about Neomuna and about the Cloud Striders represented by the damaged memorials.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Reformancer Guzheng synthesizes a droning chord under its voice as it speaks.

"The renegade Guardian has performed to expectations set by Zephyrus, Autonomous Mind," it says. "The Reformancer unit has in turn allocated a portion of our most recent shipment to the Guardian."

"As part of an ongoing social experiment, the Guzheng unit has left your goods with Spider. This unit is measuring how long he can resist the temptation to pocket the funds himself."

Guzheng's eye gleams with a threatening light. "At that point, the experiment will conclude."

The Reformancer greets you with a dramatic flourish of its garments. "This unit, designated Guzheng, currently serves as Reformancer. This title is unique and a pleasing degree of outré, just like Guzheng itself.

"You are extremely puncturable, Guardian unit. Flammable too, in our experience. Might I suggest this defensive tool? Our organization is willing to part with it as a token of equivalent exchange."

Guzheng focuses on your Exotic armor for a moment too long as you take the Deflector unit. Then its gaze snaps back to yours. "May this improve your odds."

Reformancer Guzheng unfolds itself from a crouch on your approach. 

"Zephyrus requests your assistance in trouncing our pathetic foes. Rewards are promised, as are access to desirable items and abilities.

"Have you ever thought about what it would be like to be part of the Vex? Your imagination could not simulate reality, but our Deflectors and Stun Fields may give you a taste.

"Gamble on the Reformation. Win big."
Deposit Dark Matter Ingots at the Tharsis Reformation War Chest to earn Reputation with this syndicate. Earn gear, Renegade Abilities, Praxic Blade modifications, and currency.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
The Osmic Fragment from the Wellspring seems to have a stronger pulse than the others. 

Did the Scorn's temporary possession have an effect? Or is the resonance amplified by the nearby presence of the other fragments?

More importantly, do the Scorn know what Immaru intends to do with the Osmic Fragments? They must. If they know the runes are for some kind of Lucent Brood defense, then the Osmic Fragments are undeniably part of that.

It would help if you knew the runes' specific purpose. You glance at the Hidden's open query. No progress yet. 

In the meantime, there are other angles of this case to consider. Check the other Hidden reports for more leads.

New intel awaits you on the Evidence Board. The report includes a note to Ikora:

"To IKO-006: Here's the AI-COM/RSPN protocol transcript we picked up from the wounds. According to this, before initiating YUGA SUNDOWN, Rasputin killed all protective measures in place for Human colonies and settlements. There's a big list of codenames for the Moon, Mars, Earth, the Exodus ships, et cetera… but Rasputin also refers to a place called NEFELE STRONGHOLD. No record of that in any of our databases. Forwarding to A.B. for a cross-ref."

A follow-up message from Ana Bray brings up more questions than it answers:

"To CHA-319: No hit on 'NEFELE STRONGHOLD' in any of Rasputin's records. Can't even find the original transcript you're quoting. If it's real, someone removed all traces of it. And if they did, they did it so cleanly that I'd suspect Rasputin himself."

No action items on this case; just an unsatisfying label of "UNSOLVED."

The Osmic Fragment gleams in the center of the board. Ghost's scan established that this is made of Fundamental Osmium, a super-dense transition metal found in the Throne World. 

However, it did not originate there. You spot a Hidden analysis on the material: "This particular variant sources from the planet Fundament; aka the origin world of the proto-Hive, who lived on floating elemental continents. See: the Osmium Court, birthplace of the Hive gods." 

So, Savathûn imbued her throne world with a little slice of home. But that still doesn't explain the paracausal trace lingering on these specific fragments. Nor does it account for the Lucent Brood's reaction. They definitely seemed more hostile than nostalgic… 

You consider all this as you cast your eyes over the other Hidden reports, looking for more connections.

So far, nothing else stands out. Report back later for further developments.

While some questions still linger, Ikora and her Hidden are now armed with far more answers than when they first stepped foot on the returned Mars. 

Thanks to you, the purpose of the Relic has been revealed and put to good use, Savathûn's throne world has been thoroughly investigated, and the schemes of the Lucent Brood have been officially foiled. 

And though Immaru may have escaped justice once again, the Lucent Brood won't be getting their claws on advanced weapons anytime soon. 

Speaking of, there is one more mystery you can solve. You still don't know what weapon Immaru was so desperate for. What pattern lurks within the Osmic Fragments?

Go to the Relic to shape your reward.

The complementary resonance led you to three resonant Hive runes, fiercely protected by the Lucent Brood. From there, Ghost was able to lock onto the signal of a nearby Osmic Fragment, which led directly to your prime suspect: Immaru, Savathûn's Ghost. 

What could he be planning with these Osmic Fragments? How do the resonant Hive runes fit in? Is this where the connection to the Relic lies? 

You step back and stare at the empty space on the board. Soon, it'll be filled with evidence. 

Report back later for further developments.

"I make the weapon mine. But I do not keep it… I use it as a lure." 

Savathûn was talking about the Enigma. Which you shaped with the Relic, thanks to the fragment you found on her ship.

Your mind whirrs through the logic of Savathûn's plan. By converting to the Light, she lost her memories and her Darkness-borne magic. Thus, she needed a Guardian who could harness the power of Deepsight via the Relic. 

And what better way to lure a Guardian than with the promise of a powerful weapon? 

There's an addendum to the original report: "Continued monitoring of emergent threshold (aka the Altar of Reflection) revealed previously unreported paracausal mutability, in external locational point, and presumably, internal context."

In other words, you can expect that the access point of the Altar will change—as will the tales you hear within. Still, if the Hive God of Cunning has more to say, it would be worth it to listen. 

Visit the Altar of Reflection regularly. See if you can glean the truth from Savathûn's lies.

You confirmed that the Relic, when paired with Weapon Patterns, allows the user to reach through time, rearranging memories into weaponry. There's no telling what else it can do in the hands of a powerful entity like the Witness.

Ikora posited before that the Relic caused the temporal wounds on Mars's surface. You believe she's right, and that the Witness used the device to learn about the planet's Golden Age and Collapse, leaving Mars irreversibly damaged.

Your report states that the Weapon Patterns you used are essentially Darkness-infused "memory road maps" to the weapons the Relic creates. The Osmic Fragments are a weaker, incomplete road map—but with enough fragments, someone could build the equivalent of a Weapon Pattern.

The Relic is clearly capable of anything from creating weapons to tearing the fabric of reality. If Immaru gathers enough Osmic Fragments and finds a way to approximate the functions of the Relic—perhaps by using the runes you discovered in the Throne World—there's no telling what he might create.

In the meantime, there are other angles of investigation to consider. Check the other Hidden reports for more leads.

In your explorations of the Pyramid, you've learned that the Scorn were attempting to increase their power by using resonant runes stolen from the Lucent Brood in combination with worm larvae. 

Based on the reports from those who first entered to defeat Rhulk, it seems these ritualistic experiments were a holdover from the plans of the disciple himself. 

One Hidden agent goes so far as to speculate that the Scorn Caretaker was itself the result of a successful worm-fusion.

Whatever the Scorn know of Immaru's plans, it's enough to motivate them to enhance their power further in order to counter his moves. 

The Pyramid should be continuously monitored, as the Scorn show no signs of slowing down. Visit the Pyramid regularly to clear the area.

By retracing your steps through the Throne World, you've picked up enough clues to form a theory about Immaru's motives, if not his entire plan. 

From the beginning, it was clear that the Throne World had—and still has—fierce protectors in the Lucent Brood. Their antagonism was an effective smokescreen for the fact that, behind the scenes, Savathûn actually wanted you there… 

Unlike the Scorn. You recall Immaru's voice, after you swiped the resonant runes from his squads: "We got interlopers in the area…" 

Interlopers. Not just Guardians, but any who trespass into the Throne World are the threat. 

And the defense against them lies in the Dark-tinged Osmic Fragments and the runes imbued with Hive magic. 

Just when you thought you had seen enough contradictions-in-terms in this investigation, up pops a Hive Ghost using tools of Darkness to protect a realm filled with Light. 

In the meantime, there are other angles of the investigation to consider. Check the other Hidden reports for more leads.

A new report awaits you on the Evidence Board. The Hidden have all but confirmed the emergence of a new access point to the Altar of Reflection.  

With Savathûn out of commission, this chance to delve into another of her memories is too good to pass up. 

Ikora wants you to bring the Enigma to the Altar and see if you can uncover any remaining psychic traces. The Glaive is the investigation's strongest link between the Relic and the Witch Queen.

In fact, it's the only link you have. If you're looking for answers to Ikora's lingering questions—why Savathûn chose to reappear over Mars, what her Ghost is up to, what they know about the Witness and what's to come—then the Altar is your best shot.

Bring the Enigma to the new Altar access point in the Temple of the Wrathful and see what you can uncover.

One of the files seems much denser than the others. A closer look reveals it's an abstract on Deepsight, written by Eris Morn.

"The nature of this power supports our hypothesis that Darkness is specially bound to the consciousness that stretches in webs across space and time. This makes it uniquely useful for an investigatory process. However, we have not yet fully explored its utility for reflection. 

Savathûn's Altar is one example of Deepsight's potency in this regard. The wounds spanning the desert suggest the Witness engaged in a similar process with Mars; retreading old ground to forge new paths in the future.

Of course, as Ikora is quick to note, this is a logic well-known to Guardians already, thanks to the guided battle-meditations she put into practice after the Red War. 

But now, with Deepsight… what might that practice become? What kind of insights could be mined from retracing our steps?"

You look up from the file. If Deepsight can help you glean new clues from old cases, it would be worth it to put Eris's theory to the test.

Discover new Insights by retracing your steps in weekly missions.

As you stand before the Evidence Board, a file catches your eye. It's an assessment of the Scorn presence in the Throne World, with a particularly intriguing coda:

"Our undead friends have grown smarter under their new (or rather, very old) management. One troubling example: marching orders, exhumed from an ex-Major."

You peer at the burnt page. The Eliksni-adjacent scrawl is too charred to read, but at the bottom, you spot a crude, but unmistakable drawing of… the resonant Hive rune.  

Now, why are the Scorn hunting down Hive runes? And why the specific kind that Savathûn's Ghost cares so much about?

You need to see the marching orders in full. Target Scorn elites in the Throne World to intercept their orders.

A Hidden report awaits you on the Evidence Board.

"New paracausal resonance detected in three key locations. Preliminary analysis suggests complementary match for Evidence A (aka Osmic Fragment). Telemetry linked for further analysis."

You examine the resonance comparison. The wavelengths complement each other perfectly. Where one signal dips into a valley, the other peaks, and vice versa. 

Clearly, there's something (multiple somethings) out there meant to correspond with the Osmic Fragments. Puzzle pieces meant to fit together. More proof that the Lucent Brood are planning some kind of ritual. 

Search all three areas in the Throne World for the sources of the resonance.

You walk up to the Evidence Board and select a file. It contains a message, not from Ikora or the Hidden… but Mara Sov.

"While investigating the Sunken Pyramid, I encountered Scorn amassing in large numbers within. Regardless of how many of the wretches I slaughtered, more flooded in to take their place.

With Rhulk dead, we naturally assumed they would abandon the Pyramid, but clearly they have other plans. Furthermore, they appeared to be co-opting Hive magics for reasons I was unable to decipher. Perhaps this has something to do with your ongoing investigation.

I have not the time to stay and fight; more urgent matters call my attention away. This situation, however, should be attended to promptly, as the Scorn show no signs of slowing their advance."

The Scorn using Hive magic, huh? That is curious. A lead from the Awoken Queen is certainly worth checking out.

Investigate the Sunken Pyramid in the Throne World to learn why the Scorn are rising up and how to put a stop to it.

This is the Evidence Board, the main hub of intel for the Hidden's investigations into Mars and Savathûn's throne world. 

You scan the few reports posted around the edges of the board. Clearly, Ikora's agents have been working hard, but they haven't had much luck finding concrete evidence. 

Fynch's mysterious fragment gleams darkly in your inventory. He was convinced it was linked to something shady with the Lucent Hive. And Ikora did say to log "anything of relevance" here… 

But first, you should confirm just what this fragment is. 

You've seen metallic ore similar to this in the Throne World. You should find a sample for comparison. Maybe there are others with the same paracausal resonance. 

Search the Quagmire for a sample to match the Osmic Fragment.

Thanks to the data you generated, the Hidden have found that resonant runes are essentially a Hive-magic imitation of the Relic. Which means the compatible resonance of the Osmic Fragments are actually an indication of a Weapon Pattern stored.

Or rather, a piece of one. Hence, Immaru's determination to collect all the fragments. 

Then, as soon as he'd make the pattern whole, he could use the runes to shape as many specialized weapons the Lucent Brood could ever ask for. 

If only you hadn't gotten your hands on the fragments first. Without those, Immaru will have to improvise.

And he undoubtedly will. So, Ikora proposes a turning of the tables. According to the Hidden, the shaping ritual is meant to take place in Queen's Bailey. 

Take the Osmic Fragment and use it to lure in Immaru. If you play this right, you can grab your culprit and his remaining supplies in one fell swoop.

New intel awaits you on the Evidence Board:

"Paracausal energy signatures detected in Evidence A (aka Osmic Fragment) share indeterminate link with temporal 'patterns' consumed by Artifact X (aka the Relic). So far, Evidence A elicits no response from Artifact X, but more investigation is needed."

In other words, the Darkness energy infused in the Osmic Fragments from Fynch is compatible with the Relic. Those energy readings are strikingly similar to the Weapon Patterns used to operate the Relic. The Hidden think the fragments are essentially weak, incomplete Weapon Patterns, but they need more data to be certain.

Shape more weapons using the Relic to confirm this connection. By analyzing complete Patterns, you might be able to determine whether the Osmic Fragments are truly compatible with the Relic.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Shaw Han looks at the Gjallarhorn with unrestrained awe. "The weapon of heroes," he whispers.

He pulls his eyes away from the gleaming barrel for a moment. "Guess that makes you the hero, huh?" he says with a grin. "I knew it the first time I laid eyes on you… of course, I think most of the Guardians I see are heroes. And I'm usually right."

"I have one last thing for you," he says, patting his pockets. "Hold it out, would you?"

You hold the Gjallarhorn steady and Shaw pulls something from a pouch on his belt: a small golden feather.

"I found this in the rubble of the old vaults after Ghaul's attack. I've been holding on to it ever since… for hope, I guess. To remind me of the strength of the Guardians. And now—"

He presses the gold feather into the winged wolf that adorns the Gjallarhorn. It fits into place with a satisfying click.

"—now I don't think I need a reminder," he says, then raises a fist into the sky. "Because the Guardians have the Gjallarhorn again!"

"Now get out there and let the galaxy know the big guns are back!"

Shaw takes the crumbler from you and grins. "If you've got time for baking, things must be going well for you in the Tower," he laughs.

He takes a bite. "How'd you know I love blueberries?"

"You found a full set," Shaw Han says, shaking his head in disbelief. "The Gjallarhorn reborn. I can't believe I'm going to be here for its second coming."

"But I'm getting way ahead of myself," he chuckles. "You're going to need a targeting system, armored housing, the whole deal—and I think I can help you out with one of those."

Shaw rummages through a nearby pile of gear and pulls a tarnished housing unit from near the bottom.

"I had the New Lights training with this launcher before it got dry-fired one too many times and fell to pieces. The armor's still good, though. It withstood hundreds of training rounds without so much as a crack."

"This could be the base. Think of it like you're using the strength of the new Guardians—I don't know, I'm not great at that symbolism stuff." He hands the housing to you.

"Now we need to find a gunsmith as good as Feizel Crux to piece this thing together."

He thinks to himself, then shrugs. "Banshee?" he offers. "I know the Vanguard uses him for pretty much everything, but there's a reason for that. I'm sure he'd appreciate the chance to put his mark on the next generation of the Gjallarhorn too."

"Head on up to the Tower. I'll be waiting for you… I want to be there the first time you shoot that thing!"

Shaw thanks you for your help, and apologizes for not trusting you to help him.

With the superconductor in hand, his mission is complete. Zavala has given him new orders to keep an eye on Hive and Fallen activity in the Cosmodrome, so he entrusts you to deliver the relic to the Last City.

Shaw says farewell with a final gift: Maeve's jumpship, waiting in orbit for a new pilot.

Hover over the ship icon below and select it with [Confirm], then use the Director to travel to the Last City. 

ACQUIRE SHIP

The schematic you recovered confirms Shaw's plan. An old comms array lies dormant in a nearby facility. If reactivated, it might balance the power of the superconductor enough to stop the Arc overflow.

Shaw needs to man the controls at the central power grid while you activate the array.

Hover over the weapon icon below and select it with [Confirm], then complete the mission "Cold Boot."

Shaw Han lets out a low whistle when you show him the Wolfpack Round.

"You found this under the Loot Cave? I almost can't believe I'm seeing one of these in person," he says as he carefully turns the shell over in his hands.

"I used to hear stories about the Gjallarhorn, you know. What it was capable of, that kind of thing. Never got to see one in action, though."

He pauses as a newly risen Guardian approaches. Shaw shows them how to manifest a grenade by concentrating Light in his palm. The Guardian nods and walks off, flicking their wrist.

He turns back to you. "There was meant to be a tradition where every generation of Guardians would forge their own Gjallarhorn. But then Ghaul destroyed the vaults, and with everything that's happened since then… I mean, Uldren. The Darkness. And now Savathûn…"

Shaw notices he has a white-knuckle grip on the shell. He hands it back to you.

"If you have a shell, then the Gjallarhorn never left us. Maybe it's time to bring it back."

"See what you can shake out of the Fallen scavengers around here. If you can find more traces of the original Gjallarhorn…"

"…you're about to change things for all of us."

As you offer the remains of Maeve's Ghost to Shaw, he pauses, then gestures for you to wait a moment. He pulls the edge of his cloak taut, materializes a knife, and slices a strip of cloth free.

With reverence, Shaw wraps the shards of Ghost shell in the cloth, then holds the bundle gently. 

"It's an old Hunter tradition, a way to honor lost friends. Not practiced much these days."

Looking back at you, he seems to realize something. His eyes brighten and search all around you.

"Have you felt your connection to the Traveler yet?" he asks. "I don't mean throwing purple grenades and shooting golden guns, something deeper."

Shaw tells you to find a quiet place and meditate on the Light. Strange as that sounds, he promises it will make you stronger. "Don't worry, it's not supposed to make sense."

Shaw looks you up and down as you stride into the scout post.

"I see you've made progress. I knew it would happen soon, but it's amazing to see how much you've learned." He smiles. "Not long ago, you were fresh out of the ground with only a rusty rifle to your name. Now you're on your way to mastering the powers of the Light. Ikora had better keep an eye on you. Make sure to tell her I said that next time you see her in the Last City."

Shaw looks down at his cloak, freshly mended from where it was cut earlier. 

"Just remember this power has its limits, Guardian. Keep your Ghost close at all times."

"These Fallen sure know how to keep us on our toes."

Shaw tells you that Eramis has been trying to recruit her old comrades from the former House of Devils for a while; for her to arrive in person now must mean she's growing desperate. 

Word is, she brought along a trusted sergeant, Bakris, the Adamantine, and empowered her with Stasis as a demonstration of the forces at her disposal. Shaw suspects the sergeant has remained in the Cosmodrome in order to ensure the Devils follow through on their pledge to relocate to Europa. 

Locate Bakris, the Adamantine and scatter the Devils before they leave for Europa. Defeat Fallen in the Cosmodrome, The Divide.

"Hey, Guardian! Got a minute?" Shaw Han calls as you walk up.

"You've been around the system a bit, yeah?" he asks. "Have you ever seen anything like this?"

Shaw shows you a cracked piece of crystal, faded and gray. It almost looks like—

"It almost looks like a piece of an engram, right?" Shaw says. "But dead, calcified, empty. Engrams don't act like this. Once their data is drained, they decompile. It's weird."

"A New Light brought me this. Said he found it in a little gap in the rocks not far from here… before the Red War, Guardians used to call it the 'Loot Cave.' Rumor was it was overflowing with engrams for some reason."

He shrugs. "Every piece of treasure was pulled out by Guardians long ago, though. The place is picked clean. I poke my head in from time to time on my patrols, but there's nothing left."

He turns the shard over in his hands. "Or so I thought."

"Do you think you could head to the Loot Cave and check it out for me? Any old piece of tech might help the Vanguard, and these days, we need all the help we can get."

Shaw grieves the loss of his fireteam, but the mission must continue.

He's here to find a Golden Age relic, a superconductor. If recovered, it could make a powerful weapon against the Darkness.

The superconductor is overloading the building with deadly Arc energy. Shaw needs your help figuring out a plan to get past it.

The next step is to recover intel from Fallen in the area, but first you'll need to sync with Shaw's ship to be able to relay that data back to him.

Hover over the weapon icon below and select it with [Confirm].

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Petra can't seem to tear her eyes from the bow. "The Wish-Ender. I thought it was only a legend. How did you—?"

She shakes her head once, as though snapping herself back to waking reality. "No matter. You did all that I asked and more. With their mementos purified, our honored dead can rest again."

"As for the bow…" Petra gives you a small, almost wistful smile. "I will not ask what passed between Sjur Eido and you. Hunt well, my friend."

"Your help is appreciated, as much as I wish it wasn't necessary."

Petra turns and gazes at the landscape around her, a wistful look in her eye.

"Corruption tears at the fabric of this sacred place. It pains me to see it so…"

"With your help, I am closer to cleansing this darkness, and for that, I thank you."

Destinations offer a variety of activities and rewards. Keep exploring to discover them!

Petra holds out a case full of strange mementos. Despite their small size, their antiquity is apparent—as is the Taken corruption clinging to them. Petra starts to speak, and you hear righteous anger behind her clipped words.

"These are mementos of past Awoken Paladins. I don't know how the Fallen learned of them, but a Taken attack targeted the mementos… and desecrated them."

"Our honored dead deserve better. Take their mementos into the Shattered Throne and hunt down the Taken responsible. Their blood will avenge the wrong that's been done and purify the tokens."

Petra's frown deepens. "The Fallen hid themselves well. My scouts revealed some clues, but you will have to search carefully."
Petra may not remain in one place long enough to eat the cookies you've made, but she seems quite thankful nonetheless.

"You set foot on hallowed ground, Guardian. Take care to remember that in your efforts here."

Petra Venj watches you with a steely gaze from her uncovered eye. The knife levitating above her hand flips and twirls nonchalantly.

"I swore an oath to aid my Queen, and loathe as I am to see this place tread upon by outsiders, I cannot refuse your help. The Taken and Scorn have run amok, and I don't have enough Corsairs to cover the territory."

"Do what you can against the corruption, but keep your guard up. Dark forces are at play here."

Complete public events, Lost Sectors, and bounties acquired from Petra Venj.

A brief message from Petra Venj, the Queen's Wrath, awaits you.

"The past refuses to rest peacefully here. The Taken know this as well as we do, and recent assaults targeted the very history of the Awoken."

"I won't let the Taken go unpunished. Come see me as soon as you can."

interactions.flavorLineOne:
When you approach Cayde, he motions for you to lean in close. His voice is a too-loud whisper.

"I see you got my coded message." It was just a regular message. "Listen, I've heard a thing or two about a big threat—I'm talking top priority, code red—wandering around the Pale Heart. We can't call in the big guns for this one. Gotta keep it quiet. So how's about you, me, and Crow go track it down and take it out? Quietly, remember."

All right. Nothing suspicious about this at all.

Cayde hears your approach and turns to you. He's holding a sniper rifle. While familiar in shape, its design certainly feels like Cayde has had his hands on it. He offers it to you.

"You didn't think I'd give Crow something and not cook up something for you too, right? Come onnnn," he says. "He got a shiny new cloak and, potentially, crushing responsibility. It's only fair that you get a new gun courtesy of yours truly."

Cayde crosses his arms and considers you for a moment. It feels as though the quiet is intentional, appreciating your presence, until he nods his head and pulls himself back to reality.

"It was nice gettin' into trouble with you again," he says, words laced with sincerity that lingers despite how quickly he tries to move on.

"Now, I've gotta go figure out how to get the rest of this Screeb juice out of my clothes before the big battle." Cayde sniffs his cloak, still rancid from the Screeb slime, and recoils. He whispers, "…At this point, I might just burn 'em."

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Ikora seems to be in a contemplative mood. "Much ink has been spilled about the Tenets. Can't devotion be blind, and bravery foolish? Why must we sacrifice? And why speak of death at all?"

She shakes her head slightly. "But they are not virtues, or aspirations. They are a reminder of why we are here. In the early days of the Dark Ages, there were tales of Lightbearers who turned away from the battle altogether. They reasoned that the problems of humanity did not concern them. They would endure regardless, so there was no need to form attachments to this transient world."

Then she turns to you, the corners of her mouth curving up. "So, what makes us different? It must be our devotion to others. Our compassion, justice, and love. I think the Guardians who first gave voice to the Tenets must have come to the same conclusion."

Ikora gazes serenely out at the Bazaar. As you approach, her focus sharpens on you. She smiles. 

"I still recall the day I first laid eyes on you. A New Light, still learning the powers you wielded and the responsibilities that came with them." She chuckles, perhaps remembering some misadventure. 

"I saw the spark of greatness within you, yet I could not even begin to guess who you would become. In you, the Tenets are not merely abstract ideals. They are etched into your words and deeds." Ikora's eyes glimmer with amusement. "Now, when New Lights need guidance, I am spared from lengthy lectures. I need only point to your example."

You're not entirely sure if they should be following everything you do. Ikora only smiles knowingly. "I am fortunate to know you. As a Guardian who walks with me along this path…" Her voice dips, wistful. "And as a friend."

Once again you remember how long her second life has been; how many friends she has seen come and go. 

But you are not gone. Not yet.

Ikora has analyzed the data you collected, and it all points to a single conclusion: the Vex have resurrected the Undying Mind, a Hydra built to seize control of the Black Garden. It appears to be hiding itself in multiple co-occurrent timelines. Ikora intends to devise a plan to deal with this new threat but needs time to sort out the details.

Continue your efforts in the Vex Offensive activity while Ikora develops her plan.

She and Zavala have tested the hardware extensively, locating and destroying dozens of instantiations of the Undying Mind—but there are hundreds, if not thousands, of copies still lurking in the Garden. This task now falls to you.

Enter the Black Garden to locate and defeat the Undying Mind.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Ikora is grateful for your efforts on the Moon. She has a gift for you to express that—something she thinks you might find useful.

"On behalf of the Vanguard," she says, "and…from Eris, as well."

"On behalf of the Vanguard," she says, "and…from Eris, as well."

After your adventures in the Pale Heart, Ikora seems nostalgic to be back at her post. 

"It feels strange to come back to the Tower," she says. Her tone is bittersweet. "I look over at the ramen counter and half-expect to see Cayde."

"I almost got used to having him back."

She shakes her head to clear her thoughts.

"I want to say that things will be different now… but it seems the only constant in our world is conflict. The next threat to the Vanguard could take any form, and strike at any time."

She catches herself and laughs softly. 

"Listen to me… I sound like Zavala," she says. "Time spent with old friends will do that to you."

She smiles. "When the Vanguard needs you, we know you'll be there."

"Until then."
